change: First C4 methodology. downtime_window records (C4.1, #13257) derive the complete-downtime interval by intersecting the Stage-3 S1 per-pool wall intervals [wall, reset) across every routing pool (keyed by canonical provider id), basis since_last_reset; the prediction range is [latest member wall, earliest member reset), rendered by the §4 formatter at issuance. Providers the forecast cannot project publish insufficient_history and veto a no-window verdict; a defensible no-window tick publishes no record. No day-type or spike-day adjustments (inputs.adjustments is []).
expected_effect: Downtime-window predictions exist on every gatherer tick and are scorable per design §3 (start/end error, interval overlap); §3's accuracy bar is coverage inside the calibrated band with median window error under one gatherer tick span at one-tick lead.
reason: The C4 design (doc/2026-11-13T15-12-00Z_design_reporting-architecture-event-driven/c4-forecasting-design.md, PR #13268) specifies the record, scoring, and methodology-log formats, and S1's same-period pace projection is the only measured per-pool wall source; §5 adjustments are data-gated below their sufficiency thresholds.

change: Arrival-kind rendering unified on the one shared §4 formatter (renderPredictionRange in quota-downtime.ts): model_plan_arrival records (C4.4, #13260) now store the shared formatter's renderings at issuance, replacing the arrival module's own duration/day-only copy, which had no calendar form. Stored rendered strings for arrival ranges change accordingly — a range crossing Chicago day boundaries now renders in calendar form (e.g. "between Saturday morning and Tuesday morning" in place of "between 2.5 and 5.7 days from now"), and a range whose earliest bound precedes issuance renders in calendar form instead of a negative relative duration. earliest/latest/likely instants, bases, and scoring are unchanged.
expected_effect: Arrival records render identically to downtime_window and reset_duration records for the same ranges — one §4 surface for readers and for the S7 weekly review; arrival scores remain attributable per methodology_version.
reason: Design §4 specifies one formatter producing the stored rendered string; the arrival module's duplicate had already diverged (no compound or calendar forms), so the kinds rendered the same ranges differently.

change: Shared §4 formatter dates far-out calendar bounds (#13536): a calendar-form bound a week or more from issuance now carries its month/day date after the daypart (e.g. "between Tuesday afternoon, Sep 22 and Tuesday afternoon, Oct 6" in place of "between Tuesday afternoon and Tuesday afternoon"), because a bare weekday name repeats every seven days and arrival ranges routinely span weeks. Bounds anchored to this/tomorrow/today and bounds inside one week keep their short form. Stored rendered strings change only for far-out calendar ranges; earliest/latest/likely instants, bases, and scoring are unchanged.
reason: Codex review on PR #13529 found the stored arrival rendering ambiguous for multi-week ranges; the pre-unification arrival renderer had emitted unambiguous days-from-now strings for the same ranges.
expected_effect: Far-out prediction records render unambiguously for readers, the scorer, and the C6 pages; near-horizon renderings are byte-identical to c4-meth:2 so existing scores stay comparable.

change: The §4 range formatter now implements the design as written: the day form (span ≥ 48h) is checked before the calendar form, so it can fire — previously the cross-day calendar check ran first and every ≥48h-wide range crosses a Chicago day boundary, making the day-form branch unreachable; and mixed spans render compound ("2 days 4 hours to up to 5 days 4 hours") when either bound is not an exact tenth of a day, with plain decimal days otherwise. In-progress ranges (earliest at or before issuance) still render calendar form. Downtime, reset-duration, and arrival records issued under this version carry the new renderings (arrival shares the one formatter since c4-meth:2, so its ≥48h ranges change too). Numbered c4-meth:4 on merge: main has since issued its own c4-meth:2 (arrival unification, #13408) and c4-meth:3 (far-out date suffix, #13536).
expected_effect: Prediction ranges 48h or wider render in the specified day/compound forms instead of calendar form, so stored rendered strings match §4; no change to ranges under 48h or to in-progress ranges. Re-scored by the §3 accuracy review against the ledger.
reason: The design (§4) specifies the day form for span ≥ 48h and the compound form for mixed spans, but the shipped formatter implemented neither: the day-form branch was provably unreachable and no code produced the compound form (#13357). The stored rendered string is what the scorer grades (§1), so the formatter must produce the specified forms.

change: Day-type and spike-day adjustments (C4.3, #13259 criterion 2) now compute and publish as SHADOW records (src/quota-daytype-adjustment.ts; the gatherer appends them to quota-daytype-shadow.jsonl beside the forecast product, and  reproduces them over a fixed store copy). For each pool/window with a live v1 projection, the record carries the v1 wall verbatim and the adjusted wall: the v1 pace multiplied by the measured burn-rate ratio of the Chicago cell the issuance instant falls in, at the finest grain the section 5 gate admits (precedence weekday-daypart, daypart, weekday, dayclass; a cell is admitted at >=8 independent samples counted as criterion 1 counted them, over the same rename-joined series the S2 harness assembles). Burn rates use one shared interval estimator (within reset periods, sum of delta-pct over sum of delta-t, intervals attributed to the cell of their end reading) for cell rates, the overall rate, and the spike windows. The spike-day model (S2.7) fires when the trailing-7-day rate runs >=10% under the trailing-30-day rate (long basis: >=14 distinct dates; short: >=2) and states itself explicitly: a spike_day adjustment entry, both measured rates and the light fraction on the record, and the spike wall at the adjusted pace x1.2. Cells admitted at no grain publish adjustment_unavailable with the per-grain counts. Shadow only: the published forecast is never modified and no live path reads these records; they are not written to the C4 prediction log or the quota-prediction ledger source.
reason: Criterion 1 (PR #13290) re-measured the section 5 gate over the live store: 51 of 2,583 cells admitted, all at the daypart and dayclass-weekday grains, so the models the design defines can now be built for exactly those cells; every other cell stays adjustment_unavailable until its samples cross the gate. Per section 5 earn-in, an admitted adjustment publishes as a shadow record until it beats the unadjusted forecast in the S2 harness (criterion 3, tracked on #13259).
expected_effect: Every gatherer tick now logs, per projected pool/window, the day-type-adjusted wall beside the v1 wall, so the criterion-3 harness comparison (adjusted vs unadjusted accuracy over the same history) can run on accumulated shadow records; pools whose current cell is not yet admitted keep an explicit adjustment_unavailable record instead of a silent absence.
